title: Expanding the spectrum of EEF1D neurodevelopmental disorders: Biallelic variants in the guanine exchange domain.

reviewer.method: Personally read the complete8-page main PDF via all401 layout-text lines, both complete main figures and both table pages in pixels; read the entire supplementary DOCX text and all5 rendered pages, plus full FigureS1 image. Compared both selected source-context cases and every allele/phenotype. Main PDF retrieval is inherited, not a prior reading claim; supplements newly retrieved from exact institutional route. No alternate packet is assigned for this PMID.

audit.exposure_note: Required HANDOFF reading exposed aggregate history and a historical public-control HG002/FGFR2 case-specific rank. No target-case inference ranks, inference-output files or benchmark outcome summaries consulted. This review is not blinded.

limitations: Specific mapping/wording limitation is stated above; missing findings are not negative examinations.
The paper itself explicitly says functional studies are required and c.1905+1G>A transcript testing was impossible; no variant rescue or therapeutic result is established.

Supplement labels the older Turkish daughter#2 and younger#1, reversing main Table1/Figure1; birth weights, body-measurement ages and some measurements differ across versions. Kept as internal source conflicts.
Main#2 has maternally inherited0.5Mb Xq28 duplication, absent in main#1; authors argue it does not explain severe phenotype. This does not establish universally absent alternative causes.
Supplement#4 narrative says a similarly affected cousin died, while main Table1 and main text assign death to#4. This source inconsistency is retained; no reassignment to#3.
Main Methods points to primer sequences in supplementary text, but the complete retrieved DOCX contains no primer list; both listed supplements were read, no unlisted protocol inferred.
